spec_declaration_snapshot.source: KB-2026-09-06-nuclear-envelope-shear-modulus §2: unbound from membrane.area_modulus — the nuclear envelope is TWO bilayers in parallel, so K_A = 2 x the single-bilayer value. Rawicz 2000 Biophys J 79:328 (10.1016/S0006-3495(00)76295-3, SE211, audit OK; KB-3.B1.3 verified/High) K_A = 243 mN/m +/- 10 % across 12 PCs = 2.43e5 pN/um -> 4.86e5 here. This is the GLOBAL area term (assemble.py k_area -> Surfaces.k_area, g = k_area/area0 * dA), additive to the mu_2d edge network's own areal response K_A = 2 mu_2d; the membranes are slack until envelope.excess_area = 0.30 is spent, which is why the lamina (Dahl 25 mN/m) and not the bilayers sets the measured NE stiffness. The lamina's own contribution is envelope.mu_2d + the lamina population, NOT this row.

assumptions: Two load-sharing bilayers in parallel is a model-construction assumption.
Slack, lamina and area-response definition are not measured by this arithmetic.

spec_declaration_snapshot.source: derived from Kovacs 2007 for NMII-2A ONLY (the motor is hand_kmc.NMIIA_MYOSIN; 2B's 12x would give x = 5.32 nm, f_char = 0.80 pN, OUTSIDE the KB's 1-2 pN — so the 1-2 pN agreement is a consequence of the isoform choice, not an independent confirmation): resisting 2 pN slows ADP release 5x -> x = kT ln5 / 2 pN = 3.44 nm at 310 K; the assisting 4x gives 2.97 nm, so one Bell length fits both within 15 % (it over-predicts the assisting branch by 25 %). f_char = kT/x = 1.24 pN. The SIGN is the mechanism (bonds._crossbridge: tension SLOWS the stroked state's detachment). NMIIB would be 5.3 nm. KB: SE424 Kovacs2007_PNAS, source_audit OK 2026-09-06 12:0x. Spread: the two branches of the same paper give 3.44 and 2.97 nm — 15 %

operands.note: Primary load estimates use smooth-muscle mechanics; 2 pN is not an independent NMII calibration.

spec_declaration_snapshot.source: van 't Hoff RT at 310 K: 1 mM = 2577 Pa = 2577 pN/um^2 (1 Pa = 1 N/m^2 = 1e12 pN / 1e12 um^2 = 1 pN/um^2; the row said 2.577e-3, a 1e6 unit slip, corrected 2026-09-16 Session DT; physical constant)
